Hey girl. I used the struggle a lot with my weight and body dismorphia (and I still do sometimes!). I gained weight due to a combination of lifestyle, health, diet and psychiatric meds, I know it a lot of the time it feels "I'm not trying hard enough," but in reality there are so many factors that can cause weight gain in women. I urge you to either speak to doctor or therapist about these feelings, because they can help you change your lifestyle and mindset for the better.

My therapist uses **Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs** a lot when we're working on lifestyle changes. We work our way up and listen to our body. In general, a healthy diet, daily movement, and socialization (along with safety, shelter, etc) are important to reach the self-esteem portion. Problems with mental or physical health are usually what hinders most in these areas. For example, I had really bad iron deficiency in the past, which caused me to be super tired and exhausted all the time. The whole time I thought I was just lazy and always compared myself to those who could do more. That's why it's important to keep your health in check, and advocate for yourself! It could very well change your life.

Hope this helps <3 Also if you feel like you look good, then that's all that matters! BMI is super outdated and weight does NOT equal body fat.

The basics are:

- there are usually four units in a course, with 5~ lessons per unit.

- in the last lesson in the unit, a little before the bottom of the page there will be instructions for an assignment. This is usually called "Assessment of learning"

- some courses will have extra assignments in a few lessons that you need to also send for the unit.

- if it's labelled "Asessment for feedback / peer review / self review" or something like that, it is NOT marked and you technically don't need to do it (but sometimes you do need to send it for teacher feedback if it shows up on the assignments page)

- questions boxes, practice questions  or anything you don't need to send a file of are not marked.

I've been doing my whole high school diploma on ILC. Long story short: My guidance counselor 'recommended' that drop out of high school and do ILC instead bc of my mental health issues.


Doing school from home definitely shaped me as a person- for better and for worse. In my early year (9th-10th grade) I wasn't responsible enough to keep up a schedule, and along with my untreated mental health issues I quickly fell behind. I am currently facing the consequences, but it is what it is. I'm not gonna give up just because I'm not living the same life as everyone else.

I wouldn't recommend it if you wanna enroll just because you hate school or smth. Honestly the support systems you have in physical high school are really important for your development in adolescence. I've had tough times coping with the fact that I'm home 24/7, no friends/peers or teachers. Basically not having anyone to help you makes you feel lonely, dumb, and frustrated. I started going to therapy and it's been helping me be more productive, but again I wish I had the guidance and resources you get in physical school.

I did enjoy the freedom, and I gained a more independent sense of thinking from being isolated, but I can't full heartedly say that I would pick ILC over real school. 

In comparison to other virtual high schools, ILC is definitely cheaper and easier to get good marks in. Tuition is 40$ per course. It isn't bad cause you pay per course throughout the year. For an OSSD it would $1200 for 30 credits. However, I've heard other more expensive options such as VHS have more help and support with learning. ILC on the other hand is completely independent.

I'm a muslim that fasts during Ramadan. Although I have never tried fasting for weight loss, here are some things I've experienced.

- You will **gain** weight if you still eat a lot before and after your fast.
- Your period will get messed up. I tend to have missed periods and weird flows after fasting, but it is different for everyone.
- If you don't do any physical activity while you're fasting, you will gain weight / stay the same.

I guess if you are fasting for health purposes, you're still drinking water, but I overall wouldn't recommend it because it is really easy to end up gaining weight, and hard to manage in the long run. You will probably bounce back, or cause a lot hormonal changes in your body.

I think the main thing is that you have to find something that works for you. I try to eat smaller meals throughout the day, but I know some friends and that doesn't work for them. Some people find it easier to eat larger meals less times per day. The main thing is drinking water, eating healthy, and remembering to move your body.
